title: Alias gate's len==0 skip blinds the memory-safety pin for empty-but-allocated arrays (the exact crash class it guards)
detail: Live arrays are made with capacity (core/warnings.odin: c.active = make([dynamic]Active_Crisis, 0, 1), cap 1-2; flow.drop_sites cap 8) so at len 0 raw_data is non-nil, while a correctly cloned empty array has nil data. A future shadow_clone regression omitting such a clone line aliases the live cap-N buffer, passes this gate (both len 0), and run_destroy(&clone) frees live memory — the exact 2026-08-28 SIGABRT class the gate claims to pin, silently uncaught. The comment's 'nil on both sides' premise only holds for the cloned side.
recommended_fix: Delete the len==0 early return; compare raw_data(a) != raw_data(b) unconditionally (a correctly cloned empty array is nil vs the live non-nil buffer, so the check still passes; a missed clone line now fails deterministically).
